title: Trump Needs to Channel His Inner George Costanza to End His Disastrous Iran War
author: Daniel DePetris
content:
Nearly six months into the U.S. war against Iran, one can't help but come to
the conclusion that President Donald Trump doesn't know what he's doing, is
completely out of his depth, or is basing his policy on incredibly flawed
assumptions. It brings to mind one of George Costanza's famous quotes in
'[Seinfeld](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CizwH_T7pjg)': "Every decision
I've ever made in my entire life has been wrong. My life is the complete
opposite of everything I want it to be. Every instinct I have in every aspect
of life, be it something to wear, something to eat, it's all been wrong."

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

While this might seem overly hyperbolic, it doesn't take a genius to recognize
that every decision Trump makes with respect to Iran has led to results he
didn't expect. Much like the depressed Costanza sitting in the coffee shop, an
angry Trump may now be sitting in the Oval Office wondering where it all went
wrong.
